authors: Alperen Keleş (built from cedar-policy/cedar-spec, Cedar Contributors)
title: cedar-etna, explained
h1: Cedar's verified authorization spec, turned into a bug-finding benchmark
lead: This repository is a fork of Cedar's Lean specification, the formal model behind Amazon's open-source authorization-policy language, with its machine-checked proofs: forbid always beats permit, nothing is allowed by default, validated policies can't hit type errors, and the SMT-based policy analyser is sound and complete. On top of that, Alperen Keleş's ETNA layer adds no new theorems. It adds twelve patches, each of which re-inserts a real historical bug into the code. Each patch comes with a runnable property that should catch it. Several of those bugs sit exactly where the proofs stop: the executable checks the soundness theorems assume, and the SMT-LIB text encoder and decoder that no theorem covers.
desc: An unofficial plain-English tour of alpaylan/cedar-etna: the Cedar Contributors' Lean proofs of Cedar's authorization, validation and symbolic-compilation guarantees, plus Alperen Keleş's ETNA workload, which re-injects 12 historical cedar-spec bugs and tests for them with property-based testing.
startNote: For Cedar's guarantees, start with the two authorization headlines, forbid trumps permit and default deny, then validation soundness and soundness of the equivalence check. For what this fork adds, read what ETNA adds, then testing the unverified SMT encoder and testing typechecker soundness at runtime.
sizeNote: About 98,800 lines of Lean in 355 files, almost all upstream Cedar (about 71,000 lines of proofs under Cedar/Thm). The ETNA additions are about 2,000 lines of Lean plus 12 patches. This site scans about 80 files around the headlines.
agentCtx: A fork of cedar-policy/cedar-spec (Cedar's Lean 4 specification and proofs: authorization, validation, level slicing, symbolic compilation to SMT, verification queries) extended with an ETNA property-based-testing workload of 12 re-injectable historical bugs.

gloss.List: Lean's List α: a finite ordered list. Cedar's Policies is a list of policies, and policy ∈ policies is list membership.
gloss.Bool: Lean's two-valued type true/false. A policy is satisfied when it evaluates to .ok true.
gloss.Prop: Lean's type of propositions. The predicates here (IsExplicitlyForbidden, EvaluatesTo) are Props, not runnable checks.
